title: Baremetal upgrade rollback playbook - preflight & terraform idempotency
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for performing Kubernetes control-plane and node upgrades on bare-metal / vSphere private deployments, with an emphasis on safe rollback and terraform module idempotency. The goal is to have an executable checklist that a single on-call + one operator can run safely, and that documents common pitfalls and repeatable rollback steps.

Scope:
- Applies to on-prem clusters managed by our terraform modules and kubeadm bootstrap (both vSphere and classic bare-metal PXE flows).
- Covers preflight checks, terraform best-practices for idempotency, upgrade sequence, etcd snapshot + restore, and rollback options.
- Does NOT cover re-architecting network (Calico/Cilium replacement) or major storage migrations.

Assumptions / Prereqs:
- You have console access to at least one control-plane host and one worker host.
- Terraform state is in remote backend (S3-compatible with locking) and you have credentials.
- etcd is running as static pods via kubeadm (or external etcd - call out in notes below).
- Cluster components monitored in Prometheus/Grafana and alerts firing to #infra-ops.

Quick decision matrix (upgrade vs postpone):
- If >20% worker nodes NotReady or persistent API errors -> DO NOT UPGRADE.
- If recent config drift (terraform state != live) -> reconcile first.
- If nightly release includes CRI runtime changes (containerd/CRI-O), schedule maintenance window.

Preflight checklist (execute before any change):
1) Verify cluster health (kubectl):
   - kubectl get componentstatuses || kubectl get cs (compatibility)
   - kubectl get nodes -o wide  # want all Ready and no long-term taints
   - kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide | sed -n '1,120p'
2) Check control-plane endpoints:
   - curl -k https://<api-server>:6443/healthz
   - check kube-apiserver logs for 5xx spikes (journalctl -u kubelet /var/log/pods/*)
3) Confirm etcd health and create snapshot:
   - ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key endpoint health
   - create snapshot: mkdir -p /var/backups/etcd && ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /var/backups/etcd/snap-$(date +%F-%H%M).db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key
   - copy snapshot off-host (scp) to object storage bucket and mark retention.
4) Verify backups for cluster-state:
   - terraform state pull > /tmp/state-$(date +%F).tfstate
   - export manifests: kubectl get all -A -o yaml > /var/backups/k8s-manifests-$(date +%F).yaml
5) Network and storage checks:
   - Validate CNI pods running (calico/cilium) and BGP/MTU settings consistent across nodes.
   - Check PVs: kubectl get pv | grep Bound and ensure no pending volume operations.
6) Node-level pre-checks:
   - disk space: df -h on /var/lib/kubelet and containerd dirs
   - time sync: timedatectl status or ntpq -p
   - ensure SELinux/AppArmor policy consistency (if used)
7) Terraform preflight (local):
   - terraform init -backend-config=... ; terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
   - Validate no drift: terraform plan should be empty or contain only expected changes.
   - Lock the state: ensure backend lock success before applying.

Terraform idempotency guidance (notes to module authors):
- Avoid remote-exec for imperative long-running tasks in modules; prefer null_resource with triggers for one-off hooks, and external orchestration for reboot/upgrade steps.
- Use lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true } for resources that manage instance replacement (only where safe).
- For kubelet/kubeadm config changes use a separate module that applies node config via SSH or runner job; do not let terraform attempt to drain nodes.
- Keep terraform resources small and declarative. Use data sources to read live tags/ids instead of trying to synthesize.
- When doing rolling instance replacements, encode a strict sequence in an external pipeline (GitHub Actions or Jenkins) that calls terraform apply with targeted resources.
- Always tag created AMIs/images and kubelet config changes with a changelist id + timestamp for traceability.

Upgrade sequence (control plane first, then workers):
1) Schedule maintenance window and announce to slack #infra-ops.
2) Create etcd snapshot (see preflight) and verify copy to object storage.
3) Apply control-plane kubeadm upgrade:
   - On first control-plane host: kubeadm upgrade plan
   - kubeadm upgrade apply v1.X.Y  # copy exact version string from release notes
   - Restart kubelet: systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet
   - Verify api-server endpoints return healthy, check kube-apiserver logs.
4) Sequentially upgrade remaining control-plane nodes (one at a time). Verify quorum after each node.
5) After control-plane, upgrade CRI (containerd) only if allowed by compatibility matrix. Reboot CRI and confirm nodes become Ready.
6) Upgrade kube-proxy, coredns, and CNI via manifests/helm (apply new manifests, follow rolling strategy flags).
7) Worker node upgrade: for each worker node:
   - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
   - SSH into node, apply OS/runtime updates and kubeadm upgrade steps (kubeadm upgrade node config --kubelet-version=v1.X.Y)
   - systemctl restart kubelet; crictl ps to verify runtime running
   - kubectl uncordon <node>
   - Run smoke tests on node (see validation section).

Etcd snapshot and restore (concise commands):
- Snapshot: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /var/backups/etcd/backup.db --endpoints=... --cacert=... --cert=... --key=...
- Verify: etcdctl snapshot status /var/backups/etcd/backup.db
- Restore (if needed): stop kubelet + static pods on all control-plane nodes, use etcdctl snapshot restore --name=... --initial-cluster=... --initial-cluster-state=new --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restored ... (see full reference in etcd docs).
- NOTE: Restoring etcd will change cluster state; coordinate with APISERVER endpoint updates and controller-manager. Ensure external load-balancer points to restored control-plane.

Rollback options (ordered by complexity):
1) Rollback manifests only: if only a deployment/daemonset/helm change caused issue, rollback the Kubernetes manifest via kubectl rollout undo or helm rollback.
2) Revert terraform changes: if terraform applied infra-level resource changes (e.g., machine replacement) and you have the previous state file saved, you can terraform state replace and reapply previous config. Steps:
   - terraform plan and ensure plan will recreate prior resources
   - terraform apply with caution; if state diverged, consider manual resource replacement to avoid double-destroy.
3) Etcd restore (full cluster rollback): if API-server is unhealthy due to data corruption, restore etcd from snapshot and restart control-plane. This is destructive to anything post-snapshot. Communicate widely before proceeding.

Fast restore checklist (if restoring etcd):
- Verify snapshot integrity with etcdctl snapshot status
- Stop kubelet and kube-apiserver pods on ALL control-plane nodes
- Move /var/lib/etcd -> /var/lib/etcd.bak before restore
- Run etcdctl snapshot restore ... with correct initial-cluster flags
- Start control-plane components and validate quorum
- Reconcile external load-balancer endpoints if client certs changed

Validation & smoke tests (post-upgrade):
- kubectl get cs; kubectl get nodes
- kubectl get pods -A | grep -E "CrashLoopBackOff|Completed" # investigate
- Basic app smoke test anchored in CI: run curl against 2-3 service endpoints behind the LB, check latency & 200
- Run cluster-health script: ./scripts/cluster-health.sh --kubeconfig /path/to/kubeconfig (script checks DNS, service IPs, API latency)
- Run an automated e2e subset (not full k8s conformance) focused on our critical paths: auth, inference microservice, persistent storage mount.

Observability & Metrics to watch during upgrade (first 30 min):
- API server request-duration p50/p95: alert if p95 > 2s
- Apiserver 500s increase
- Etcd leader changes (too many leader changes = unstable)
- Node NotReady count
- Pod restart rate (increased restarts need tracing)

Common gotchas & lessons learned (notes):
- vSphere clusters can lose time sync after upgrades; double-check vCenter NTP settings.
- Terraform module that reboots nodes via remote-exec caused partial drains — prefer external orchestration for node reboots.
- CNI upgrades are the most likely cause of broad disruption; always run CNI upgrade in a test cluster first and have rollbacks for CNI manifests.
- Kernel/CRI combos: ensure containerd version matches compatibility matrix for the kubelet being installed.

To-do / Open questions (for next revision):
- Add an automated test harness to replay a staged terraform apply in a disposable env before prod apply. (INF-2137)
- Decide on permanent strategy for machine replacement: terraform-native vs. external ephemeral runner.
- Add explicit how-to for on-prem UI access (IPMI/iDRAC steps) in the event a node fails to boot after upgrade.

Appendix: example terraform snippet (idempotent pattern suggestion)
# Keep as multiline text to copy into module README
variable "node_image_tag" {
  description = "Cluster node image tag; bump to roll nodes with new image"
  type        = string
  default     = "2025-11-01-base"
}
resource "vsphere_virtual_machine" "node" {
  # ... trimmed for brevity ...
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
    ignore_changes = [
      # kubelet config file managed by config-management pipeline, not TF
      file_paths
    ]
  }
}

Notes to self (informal):
- If anything looks off, STOP and escalate to on-call infra SRE. Dont try to patch multiple things at once.
- Keep a running log of each action in the incident ticket; timestamps are critical for root cause analysis.

References:
- kubeadm upgrade docs: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubeadm/kubeadm-upgrade/
- etcd snapshot docs: https://etcd.io/docs/v3.5/op-guide/snap/
- Internal PR (upgrade harness): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-private/pull/412

End of draft playbook.
